Jot guides

  • Writing in Jot: how to write a .jot journal by hand: dates, tasks, notes, ratings. Ten minutes; the first section is enough to start.
  • Using the template editor: design a journal's shape and download it as a .jot file to fill in, on a computer, a phone or InkDeck.
  • Write your own manual: one page that says why you keep a journal, what you do, what your marks mean and how you start again after a gap. The template editor writes half of it for you.
  • Converting an old diary: turn a diary kept as plain text (your own, or one from Project Gutenberg) into dated Jot entries.

To see Jot at length, the Examples page has whole public-domain diaries converted to .jot.

These guides are also pages on the site (/guide/), built from these files by site/build-guides.mjs. The full rules are in the Jot specification.
